text:
maya: FYI after enabling the new fast FP8 matmul path in staging I see small but growing output drift on long-context chat evals. Not huge for single-step, but by ~1k tokens the assistant hallucinated repeated phrases.

jordan: can you paste the exact flag/commit?

maya: enabling `ENABLE_FP8_FAST=1` + runtime rev a3c9f2. Repro script: `pytest tests/e2e/quant_activation_repro.py::test_long_chat_repro -k smoke`

sam: quick numbers? perf looked good right?

maya: perf: p50 token latency ~unchanged, throughput +12% under load. But model log-prob checks show cumulative KL drift vs baseline; checksum diff after 1024 tokens: `sha256sum: baseline: e3b0c4..., fp8fast: d41d8c...` (sample attached).

li: is this only when KV is enabled / cache hits?

maya: good call — repro is deterministic when KV cache reuse is on. If we clear cache every step outputs match. So seems related to cached activation quantization + accumulation.

jordan: likely the new kernel does a slightly different accumulation/rounding on the activation scale when merging KV blocks. Maybe the per-block requantization uses fp16 intermediate instead of bf16 on that codepath.

sam: can we get a tiny profile + flame for the matmul path? devops-bot, can you run a perf job?

devops-bot: perf job queued: run/1901234567-fp8-fast-profiling. ETA ~ 20m.

(20m later)

devops-bot: profiling done: https://perf.dev/internal/1901234567-fp8-fast-profiling (summary: fast-kernel hot, KV-merge code 18% of token time).

jordan: looking at the code, the fast path uses fused `scale->quantize->matmul` with a shared scale register. I wonder if the scale clipping threshold differs from the reference path (ref path clamps at 2^15, fast path at 2^14). small difference could bias rounding.

li: also seen similar symptom when we previously switched INT8 kernels — boundary quant table differences produce tiny biases that accumulate on long sequences. Two things to try: match scale/clamp constants exactly and add deterministic rounding (stochastic rounding can help unbiased but breaks determinism).

maya: I ran a quick patch to sync clamp constants to ref path in staging and the repro drops from divergence at 1k tokens to divergence at ~4k tokens. So that moved the needle.

jordan: good. two follow-ups: 1) add unit test that runs a long-token golden-checksum with KV reuse (nightly), 2) instrument per-token scale values to catch creeping bias.

sam: also add a canary rollout: flip the kernel on only 1 instance behind a canary route and run synthetic long-chats to catch this in e2e before full rollout.

maya: opened GH #487: "activation-quant: FP8-fast scale clamp mismatch causes long-chat drift" with repro + logs. Assigned to @jordan.

jordan: I will bisect kernel changes and add a patch to align clamp and quantization rounding. Quick bandaid: we can force KV merges to use reference requant path until fix lands.

li: small note — we should also check mixed-precision path where queries are BF16, keys cached in FP16 and then quantized; path permutations are many. I can add a param matrix test in the quant perf harness.

sam: priority? this can affect production long-conversation customers. Recommend P1 for the kernel fix + canary.

maya: agreed. I'll monitor canary once 1st patch is in. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

jordan: tracking branch `fix/quant-scale-unify` -> will send PR with tests.

(reacts)
maya: :eyes:

sam: added a nightly job `nightly/quant-activation-longchat` to catch regressions automatically.

li: note for postmortem: add a short doc explaining how quant clamp/scale differences accumulate over cache reuse — helped me debug quicker next time.

maya: cool. leaving logs and repro in the GH issue. If anyone hits related noise in perf dashboards ping me.
